PROJECT & OPERATIONAL KNOWLEDGE
Project Technical Specification: Enterprise Knowledge
Assistant
System Architecture, Semantic Chunking, Hybrid Vector Store, and Grounded RAG Pipeline
System: Python 3.11 / Django / pgvector
Version: 2.4
Owner: AI Architecture Core
Status: Active Production
1. System Overview and Business Context
The Enterprise Knowledge Assistant (EKA) is Apex Global Technologies' internal conversational intelligence platform.
EKA ingests, indexes, and queries our vast institutional corpus—comprising HR policies, IT security standards,
engineering documentation, operational SOPs, and system postmortems—enabling employees to obtain authoritative,
grounded, and verified answers with precise source citations.
2. End-to-End Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Architecture
Core Query Solution: Technologies & RAG Pipeline Mechanics
Which technologies does EKA use, and how does its RAG pipeline work?
EKA is constructed on a high-performance stack: Python 3.11, Django 4.2 REST Framework, Celery + Redis,
PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector, and Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet / OpenAI text-embedding-3-large. Its operational
RAG pipeline executes in six discrete phases:
Document Ingestion & Parsing: Files (PDF, Markdown) uploaded via API are parsed using PyPDFium2 and
Markdown-it. Tables and structural headings are normalized into Markdown syntax.
Semantic Chunking: Text is partitioned into 512-token chunks with 50-token sliding overlap, preserving
document metadata (title, section headers, doc_id, category).
Vector Embedding: Each chunk is converted into a 3072-dimensional vector using OpenAI's 
text-embedding-3-large model.
Hybrid Search (Dense + Sparse): Queries trigger parallel retrieval across PostgreSQL 15: 
Dense Vector Search: Cosine similarity search using pgvector with HNSW indexing.
Sparse Lexical Search: Keyword search using PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector with BM25 ranking).
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): Merges top-50 vector and top-50 keyword matches into a unified candidate
pool.
Cross-Encoder Re-Ranking: The candidate pool is evaluated by BAAI/bge-reranker-large , returning the top-5
highest-scoring relevant chunks.
Grounded Generation with Strict Citations: An LLM prompt injects the top-5 chunks into Claude 3.5 Sonnet
(temperature 0.1). The model must cite exact sources ( [Document_Name, Section, Page] ) for every claim. If
ungrounded, it states that information is not available.
